bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Read the second time. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 10.
bill.officialSummary: Laken Riley Act This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to detain certain non-U.S. nationals ( aliens under federal law) who have been arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. The bill also authorizes states to sue the federal government for decisions or alleged failures related to immigration enforcement. Under this bill, DHS must detain an individual who (1) is unlawfully present in the United States or did not possess the necessary documents when applying for admission; and (2) has been charged with, arrested for, convicted of, or admits to having committed acts that constitute the essential elements of burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. The bill also authorizes state governments to sue for injunctive relief over certain immigration-related decisions or alleged failures by the federal government if the decision or failure caused the state or its residents harm, including financial harm of more than $100. Specifically, the state government may sue the federal government over a decision to release a non-U.S. national from custody; failure to fulfill requirements relating to inspecting individuals seeking admission into the United States, including requirements related to asylum interviews; failure to fulfill a requirement to stop issuing visas to nationals of a country that unreasonably denies or delays acceptance of nationals of that country; violation of limitations on immigration parole, such as the requirement that parole be granted only on a case-by-case basis; or failure to detain an individual who has been ordered removed from the United States.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to detain individuals who are in the country without authorization and have been arrested for or charged with burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. It would also allow state governments to sue the federal government for injunctive relief when federal immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing individuals from custody or not fulfilling visa or asylum processing requirements—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates new litigation exposure for federal agencies, affecting federal and state government operations and budgets.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, increasing demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would require Homeland Security to detain certain people who are not U.S. citizens ( aliens under federal law) who have been arrested for burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting.
plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in an application, and how long it takes. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
